applicable_when: This kernel performs a strided memory transpose: input tensor has layout (N,C,H,W) with strides (4032000,1,32000,128) — channels are stride-1 (innermost). The load address `in_ptr0 + (y0 + 128*x2 + 4032000*y1)` means consecutive threads in the warp (varying xindex) access addresses 128 floats=512 bytes apart, causing severe non-coalesced scalar loads. Every load misses L1 (0% hit rate) and hammers L2 (96.87% throughput). Adding tl.multiple_of and tl.max_contiguous hints on the load offset tells the Triton compiler that accesses are aligned and contiguous within a tile, enabling 128-bit (float4) vectorized loads instead of scalar 32-bit loads. This reduces memory transactions by up to 4x and alleviates the L2 bottleneck. @triton.autotune explores XBLOCK/YBLOCK/num_warps/num_stages to find the optimal tile shape.
